summary: Mistral released Leanstral 1.5, an Apache-2.0 licensed, 119B-total/6B-active-parameter model specialized for formal proof engineering in Lean 4, available via Hugging Face and a free API.

mechanisms.reason: The model uses a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture with far fewer active than total parameters, reducing per-token compute relative to a dense model of similar total size.
mechanisms.quote: a free Apache-2.0 licensed model with 119B total and only 6B active parameters

mechanisms.reason: The model is shown spending dramatically more test-time compute per task as the token budget rises, with performance scaling smoothly up to very large budgets.
mechanisms.quote: performance climbs smoothly and monotonically the whole way, from 44 problems solved at 50k to 244 at 200k, 493 at 1M, and 587 at 4M

mechanisms.reason: The model sustains reasoning and file-editing across millions of tokens with repeated context compaction, indicating heavy KV-cache and context-memory demand during inference.
mechanisms.quote: Over 2.7 million tokens and 22 compactions, Leanstral systematically unfolded each layer of the TimeM monad

practices.reason: A team doing formal verification or proof-assisted code review could adopt this open-weights model given its stated state-of-the-art results on math and code-verification benchmarks, though it is niche relative to general-purpose model use.
practices.quote: Leanstral 1.5 saturates miniF2F, solves 587/672 PutnamBench problems, and achieves a new state-of-the-art of %87 on FATE-H and 34% on FATE-X

practices.reason: The lab open-sources FLTEval, a benchmark based on real pull requests, giving engineering teams a concrete, runnable instrument for measuring proof-engineering competence.
practices.quote: With this release, we also fully open source FLTEval

practices.reason: The described code-agent loop with real-time Lean language server inspection and multi-round context compaction is a concrete agent-scaffolding pattern a team could adapt for long-horizon verification tasks.
practices.quote: it edits files, runs bash commands, and uses the Lean language server to inspect goals, errors, and type information in real time
